master.definition_en: The sudden onset of inflammation of heart muscle with myocellular necrosis; this is generally secondary to an infectious cause, and patients often have a recent history of a flu-like illness.

curated.lethality_detail_zh: 多由病毒感染诱发过度固有免疫与‘细胞因子风暴’，导致心肌细胞广泛水肿坏死；起病极急、进展迅猛，常在数小时至数天内（多为起病24–72小时）迅速恶化为难治性心源性休克、恶性室性心律失常/三度房室传导阻滞及多器官功能衰竭；传统治疗下院内病死率曾高达50%–70%以上。
curated.treatability_summary_zh: 极具特征性的‘只要撑过急性期即常可完全痊愈’急症！采用中国《成人暴发性心肌炎诊断与治疗中国专家共识/指南（2024）》‘以生命支持为依托的综合救治方案’（极早期IABP/ECMO+足量糖皮质激素+足量IVIG），可将院内病死率从50%以上压降至5%以下，绝大多数幸存者心功能完全恢复正常。

annual_deaths_global.range_or_note: GBD 2021统计全球全部心肌炎年死亡约31,765例（ASDR约0.40/10万人；暴发性心肌炎为急性重症高危亚型，未在GBD中单独拆分，BMJ Heart / GBD 2021）

annual_deaths_china.range_or_note: 中国无全国全人群单列死亡总数；但全国推广中华医学会心血管病学分会（CSC）‘以生命支持为依托的综合救治方案’后，大型心脏中心成人暴发性心肌炎院内病死率已从传统>50%降至<5%（CSC 2024指南）
annual_deaths_china.source: 《成人暴发性心肌炎诊断与治疗中国指南（2024）》PMID:38332216

epidemiology.prevalence_global: GBD 2021全球心肌炎年新发约 132 万例（ASIR 16.16/10万人）、现患逾 50.5 万例，男性负担高于女性；其中约5%–10%的急性心肌炎表现为暴发性病程
epidemiology.prevalence_china: 全年均可散发（青壮年及儿童青少年高发），常有上呼吸道或肠道病毒前驱感染史，早期易被误诊为‘胃肠炎’或‘重感冒’

clinical_management.acute_emergency_protocol_zh: 严格执行中国CSC 2024指南核心原则——‘早识别、让心脏休息、控免疫风暴’：1）尽量减少正性肌力药与大剂量升压药对受损心肌的二次做功损伤；2）极早期启用机械循环支持（首选主动脉内球囊反搏IABP，效果不佳或严重休克/恶性心律失常立即联合VA-ECMO）及临时心脏起搏；3）早期足量免疫调节：静脉甲泼尼龙冲击（如200mg/d起视体重与炎症风暴快速压制）联合大剂量静脉丙种球蛋白（IVIG 10–20g/d×3–5天）；4）合并呼吸/肾衰竭行无创/有创通气及CRRT。

research_progress.breakthroughs_and_trials_zh: 由中国学者（汪道文教授团队及中华医学会心血管病学分会）牵头制定并在国际推广的《成人暴发性心肌炎诊断与治疗中国指南（2024）》（PMID:38332216），通过临床队列证实‘生命支持（IABP/ECMO）+足量激素+IVIG’可将病死率从>50%降至<5%，成为急性心肌炎救治的国际中国方案；在免疫检查点抑制剂相关暴发性心肌炎（ICI myocarditis）领域，阿巴西普（Abatacept）与鲁索替尼（Ruxolitinib）正展开靶向T细胞共刺激/JAK通路的临床研究。
research_progress.key_unmet_needs_zh: 1）早期症状酷似普通感冒或急性胃肠炎，基层医院极易延误至心跳骤停才确诊；2）对免疫检查点抑制剂（肿瘤免疫治疗）诱发的致死性暴发性心肌炎尚需精准靶向生物制剂；3）部分地区ECMO及跨院转运能力不足。

master.definition_en: An unusual benign or malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic large polygonal cells with granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm which contains abundant lysosomes. It was originally thought to be a tumor originating from muscle cells and was named granular cell myoblastoma. Subsequent studies have suggested a derivation from Schwann cells. master.definition_en: Granuloma annulare is a long-term (chronic) skin disease consisting of a rash with reddish bumps arranged in a circle or ring. The most commonly affected areas are the forearms, hands and feet. The lesions associated with granuloma annulare usually resolve without treatment. Strong steroids (applied as a cream or injection) are sometimes used to clear the rash more quickly. Most symptoms will disappear within 2 years (even without treatment), but recurrence is common. The underlying cause of granuloma annulare is unknown.

mechanisms: Tyrosine-protein kinase TYK2 negative allosteric modulator

master.definition_en: A rare subtype of CMT1 characterized by a variable clinical presentation. Onset within the first two years of life with a delay in walking is not uncommon; however, onset may occur later. CMT1E is caused by point mutations in the PMP22 (17p12) gene. The disease severity depends on the particular PMP22 mutation, with some cases being very mild and even resembling hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies, while others having an earlier onset with a more severe phenotype (reminiscent of Dejerine-Sottas syndrome) than that seen in CMT1A, caused by gene duplication. These severe cases may also report deafness and much slower motor nerve conduction velocities compared to CMT1A patients.

master.definition_en: A life-threatening condition that can potentially complicate pregnancy. It is named for 3 features of the condition: H emolysis, E levated L iver enzyme levels, and L ow P latelet levels. It typically occurs in the last 3 months of pregnancy (the third trimester) but can also start soon after delivery. A wide range of non-specific symptoms may be present in women with HELLP syndrome. Symptoms may include fatigue; malaise; fluid retention and excess weight gain; headache; nausea and vomiting; pain in the upper right or middle of the abdomen; blurry vision; and rarely, nosebleed or seizures. The cause of HELLP syndrome is not known, but certain risk factors have been associated with the condition. It is most common in women with preeclampsia or eclampsia. If not diagnosed and treated quickly, HELLP syndrome can lead to serious complications for the mother and baby.The main treatment is to deliver the baby as soon as possible, even if premature. Treatment may also include medications needed for the mother or baby, and blood transfusion for severe bleeding problems.

master.definition_en: A rare, genetic, isolated diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma characterized by diffuse, mild to thick, finely demarcated hyperkeratosis of palms and soles. master.definition_en: A rare genetic disorder with an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance. It is caused by the ineffective or decreased biosynthesis of the third complement component, C3. C3 deficiency may also be acquired acutely post-infection or chronically from co-morbid autoimmune disorders. If C3 is adequately synthesized, its rapid depletion may result in a functional deficiency. Clinical signs of the inherited deficiency present within the first decade of life and are consistent with the signs of recurrent systemic infection or immune complex disease. Deficiency of serum C3 and its major cleavage product, C3b, will decrease the effective humoral immune response to encapsulated bacteria. Deficiency of C3 also impairs clearance of circulating immune complexes and therefore predisposes to rheumatic and renal disease.

mondo_categories: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism

master.definition_en: A rare benign renal tumor characterized by a typically unilateral, solitary, multiloculated cystic mass consisting of small, non-communicating cysts with flat, cuboidal, or hobnail epithelial lining, separated by fibrous septa which may have an ovarian stroma-like appearance or be paucicellular. The tumor is surrounded by a thick fibrous capsule and does not contain solid areas or necrosis. Patients may be asymptomatic or present with a palpable abdominal mass and/or abdominal or flank pain. Age distribution is bimodal, the typical age of onset being either below five or between 40 and 70 years of age.

master.definition_en: A rare, congenital non-syndromic heart malformation characterized by an abnormal shunting between the left ventricle and right atrium. The clinical manifestation varies, depending on the volume of the shunt. Small congenital shunts are usually asymptomatic or associated with dyspnea and fever, whereas larger shunts often present with chest pain, fatigue, weakness, lower extremity edema, and sometimes heart failure and death. Other congenital heart anomalies may be associated.

master.name_en: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy
master.definition_en: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TSEN2 gene. This condition is associated with intellectual disability, growth delay, hypotonia, motor delay, ataxia, vision issues, cardiac features (including left ventricular hypertrophy), and pulmonary complications (such as acute respiratory distress and edema). It is also linked to brain structural anomalies such as pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, cortical atrophy, and dilated ventricles. Renal features include proteinuria, thrombotic microangiopathy, end-stage kidney disease, and high-severity hypertension.
synonyms_en: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy

master.definition_en: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCB1 gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to schwannomas, meningiomas, rhabdoid tumors and other rare types of tumors. The phenotype correlates with the variant's degree of loss of function: the schwannomatosis phenotype is more commonly observed with partial loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants, while the rhabdoid tumor phenotype is more commonly associated with complete loss-of-function variants.
